newsitem.title: USA: Disney signs long term pact with Telepiu.
newsitem.headline: Disney signs long term pact with Telepiu.

text.p: Walt Disney Co. said Wednesday it signed a long-term pay-per-view and exclusive pay television agreement with Italian pay television service Telepiu. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The move is the latest in a series of agreements between Hollywood studios and European broadcasting companies looking to acquire American films and television programmes to feed their growing satellite networks.
Disney/ABC International Television said that under the agreement, which will run for 10 years, it will license pay television and pay-per-view rights to Telepiu for live action feature films.
Telepiu also will carry a newly developed premium Disney channel for Italy on Telepiu's satellite starting in late 1997.
Telepiu, Italy's pay television operator, recently launched a digital direct home satellite service, Telepiu Satellite.
The service currently offers six channels in its basic tier, three premium channels and Telepiu Calcio, featuring Italian league soccer.
In January, Telepiu will expand with four new thematic channels and three premium channels for movies and sports when Telepiu's four additional transponders are operational.
Based in Milan, Telepiu is owned by Dutch-based media group Nethold, the Kirch Group and Fininvest.
Nethold recently agreed in principle to merge with French pay TV channel Canal Plus.
On Tuesday, Canal Plus entered into a long-term agreement with News Corp. unit 20th Century Fox allowing it to have rights for all Fox films for encrypted broadcasts.
